title: [finding] fleet-write `issue_create` read-back reports UNVERIFIED ("no issue created") for issues that were created: 2 of this shift's 4 card filings, so every such miss costs a manual board read
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site.** This is a handover-report item (`seat-lifecycle.md`: a mechanizable item goes to the skills lane as a `finding`).
- **Reader:** the skills seat. It edits `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` `readBackStroke`, the `issue_create` branch (about `:681`–`:697` at `origin/main`).
- **Dedupe:** a semantic issue search for "fleet-write issue_create read-back UNVERIFIED no issue created race", open and closed, returned 1 hit, the unrelated #8374.

## What happened

`domain:devx` seat 2 (`session_01JAhu8u8QfBvRjVZDox7CP9`) filed 4 cards through `scripts/pm/issue-create.mjs` on 2026-10-01. Two of them came back:

> `✗ issue-create: relay run FAILED — conclusion success, but UNVERIFIED — action 1 (issue_create): no issue created on objectstack-ai/objectstack since the dispatch carries the title sent`

Both issues had in fact been created, each with the exact title sent:
- Relay run `36824566714` → #21096.
- Relay run `36835496924` → #21127.

The other two filings (#21114 and #21135) read back as `IDENTICAL`.

## Why it is a defect, not noise

The tool fails safe. It does not retry, and it tells the operator to read the run and the board, which this seat did both times. The cost is the false negative itself.
- Each one makes the operator stop and read the board by hand.
- An operator who trusts the verdict and files again gets a duplicate card.

Fifty percent false negatives in one shift is a reading the operator cannot trust.

## Mechanism (read, not measured)

The branch lists `GET /repos/{repo}/issues?state=all&sort=created&direction=desc&since=…`, then judges `unfound` on the first pass when no title matches. Two things are worth checking:
- **List lag:** a just-created issue missing from the list endpoint for a few seconds after the run concludes. Nothing re-lists before the verdict.
- **`since` semantics:** `since` filters on `updated_at`, and the page budget is 3. That should still include a brand-new issue, so lag is the stronger suspect.

A pin could replay a listing that lacks the issue on the first call and has it on the second, and expect `IDENTICAL`, not `unfound`.

## Done when

An `issue_create` read-back re-lists, with a bounded wait, before it returns `unfound`, and a test pins that path. The existing "⛔ not retried; read the board" stop stays for a genuine miss.
